[Feralae-emerald-dream](https://eu.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Feralae-emerald-dream) January 27, 2024, 5:43pm 1

Blizzard should ban all addons and manually review each addon that devs want to add.  
There should be a seperate section on the Battlenet launcher for only approved addons.  
Addons should remain free and there should be an optional “Donate” option to support addon devs.  
Alternatively they could run ads on that addon section with a % of the earning going to the devs.

Feralae:
> Blizzard should ban all addons and manually review each addon that devs want to add.

[Feralae-emerald-dream](https://eu.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Feralae-emerald-dream) January 27, 2024, 9:49pm 13

From what I know, certain Bot programs hide in plain site. That being the addon folder.  
The bot can be named anything so if Blizzard were to look into someone’s account who they suspect is botting and see nothing but the usual addons and a slightly abnormal gaming pattern wouldn’t necessarily break grounds for banning them and the bot continues to roam free.  
The majority of banned bots that Blizzard cares enough to inform us about are the obvious flyhacking and brainless bots that are reckless and easy to spot.
Any other bot that is slightly more careful can be mistaken as a player no problem whatsover.  
Obviously not all bots use this addon tech and prioritize harder to detect methods but it doesn’t make it any less of a threat.  
So this is my solution; restrict addons to ONLY approved ones.  
Almost every other game restricts addons and mods because it knows how much of a risk it is to have such an “open border” policy with their game. And here we are with bots running rampant and thousands of addons that create an impossible game of player ingenuity vs dev game design.

[Linalool-1448](https://eu.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Linalool-1448) (Linalool) January 27, 2024, 10:01pm 14

Feralae:

> From what I know, certain Bot programs hide in plain site. That being the addon folder.
> The bot can be named anything so if Blizzard were to look into someone’s account who they suspect bots seeing nothing but the usual addons and a slightly abnormal gaming pattern wouldn’t necessarily break grounds for banning them and the bot continues to roam free.  
> The majority of banned bots that Blizzard cares enough to inform us about are the obvious flyhacking and brainless bots that are reckless and easy to spot.  
> Any other bot that is slightly more careful can be mistaken as a player no problem whatsover.  
> Obviously not all bots use this addon tech and prioritize harder to detect methods but it doesn’t make it any less of a threat.  
> So this is my solution; restrict addons to ONLY approved ones.  
> Almost every other game restricts addons and mods because it knows how much of a risk it is to have such an “open border” policy with their game.
And here we are with bots running rampant and thousands of addons that create an impossible game of player ingenuity vs dev game design.
> 
>

I think you misunderstand what WoW addons are. WoW Addons are text files, where as that you describe are binary files. I’m sure Blizzard would check for binary files in the addons folder. WoW wont load binary files just because they are in the addon folder.

As others have described, addons can only do what Blizzard allows through the LUA API.

[Feralae-emerald-dream](https://eu.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Feralae-emerald-dream) January 27, 2024, 10:07pm 15

Just gonna q Google on this one:

" PixelBot is a combination of an addon and a python program that exploits WoW API in order to automate characters and play the game alone"

[SteveKar-834677](https://eu.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/SteveKar-834677) (SteveKar) January 27, 2024, 10:08pm 16

Yeah I think as said above you are fundamentally misunderstanding how addons work.
Addons are text files that use a language to do certain things that wow allows. What wow allows is only the display of certain information from the game.  
That means that any addon is incapable of executing any action by itself (just display information on your ui), or change the appearance of your ui.

Also, blizzard has problems with finding bot because they cannot have access to the rest of the computer to scan for weird files. They HAVE those permissions in the wow folder, so that would make it easy as heck to find said bots.

Feralae:

> Almost every other game restricts addons and mods because it knows how much of a risk it is to have such an “open border” policy with their game.
> 
>

As said above, it is not an open border policy, just because they monitor how the addons can communicate with the game.

All things considered, what you are describing cannot be done with addons.

Feralae:

> Just gonna q Google on this one:
>
> " PixelBot is a combination of an addon and a python program that exploits WoW API in order to automate characters and play the game alone"
> 
>

The addon part is to “read” what is happening on the screen (in this case the hekili addon), which can be replicated to work without addons (through screen capture). The “bot” part is the key presser that is working outside wow to replicate your key presses.

1 Like

[Linalool-1448](https://eu.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Linalool-1448) (Linalool) January 27, 2024, 10:10pm 17

Feralae:

> Just gonna q Google on this one:
> 
> " PixelBot is a combination of an addon and a python program that exploits WoW API in order to automate characters and play the game alone"
> 
>

**Emphasis on python** , not addon. Mods are not allowed by Blizzard and have nothing to do with LUA addons.

World of Warcraft Forums

# Add-on Policy Clarification

Community General Discussion

[Nephilite-zuljin](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Nephilite-zuljin) (Nephilite) February 10, 2022, 2:59pm 1

Why are certain add-ons still allowed to operate with “premium features requiring money” when such practices are prohibited by Blizzard’s own add-on policy? I love the add-on, but TSM comes to mind as a major offender of this, and certainly not the only add-on that does. With the recent add-on manager news in the community, I feel like this is as good a time as any for the community to be given some clarification on Blizzard’s add-on policies. Don’t get me wrong, I would hate to lose access to some of these add-ons (I’m using over 50 add-ons on my Paladin right now, in fact). That being said, I recognize the importance of elucidating policies within a community and believe it’s imperative now more than ever.
Blizzard, please let us know which policies you intend to enforce and which policies you plan to not enforce.

Thanks!

5 Likes

[Ragefury-blackwater-raiders](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Ragefury-blackwater-raiders) February 10, 2022, 3:03pm 2

It’s kind of a grey area. They aren’t selling the addon, they are selling the data the addon uses. A lot of the wow pilot guides do this. Honestly, I think Blizzard should crack down on this.

18 Likes

[CutiePi-2727634](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/CutiePi-2727634) (CutiePi) February 10, 2022, 3:06pm 3

[Naiamaia-1879473](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Naiamaia-1879473) (Naiamaia) February 10, 2022, 3:30pm 5

Same thing with ppl like Overwolf profiting on Addon gatekeeping.

This all needs a crack down.  
if “boosting communities” were ALL bad; then addon-gatekeeping in any shape is also ALL bad.

Going to add it here too:  
Blizz need to make their own addon helper to curb the issue, or make the game more comprehensive on its own and not rely on addons, or give addons so much power, to present the game in a more informative way.

I also argue the game itself is getting too complex, but that’s opinion based.

Also:  
I rather download addons on my own than use Overwolf and support that gatekeeping idiocrazy.

6 Likes
[Fence-1382739](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Fence-1382739) (Fence) February 10, 2022, 3:31pm 6

Hycendia:

> Same thing with ppl like Overwolf profiting on Addon gatekeeping.
> 
>

Who is going to host a data center with millions of monthly visitors/downloads…without any method to cover thier server fees or operating costs?

Both Overwolf and WoWUp (soon) will be generating revenue through ads. That is no where close to the same as charging a fee

Also, as many have pointed out in other threads…you are free to download your own addons without using the clients

2 Likes

[Naiamaia-1879473](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Naiamaia-1879473) (Naiamaia) February 10, 2022, 3:36pm 7

Addons used to be based on love for the game and the craft, not making profits.  
That was the original idea of even allowing addons.

...

I also added to this post how I do prefer downloading on my own if this is what it comes to, I had this in another post - just not this one, so I apologize for the confusion)

4 Likes

[Fence-1382739](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Fence-1382739) (Fence) February 10, 2022, 3:41pm 8

Hycendia:

> “Who is going to” – stop you right there bud — Blizzard, if they wish to continue relying their game on Addons so much to make it function in any sane form.
> 
> (actually misremembered which post it was, however; Blizz should make their own addon-helper is part of my argument.)
> 
>

I’m going to disagree.

Blizzard has botched everything that they have touched in recent history so I do not feel giving them direct control of addons is a good idea.

Also, I really enjoy the ability to fully customize my game play and UI through addons so Blizzard removing addons amd forcing the use of whatever addons they have decided to integrate sounds horrible.

1 Like
[Tahbitha990-1519792](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Tahbitha990-1519792) (Tahbitha990) February 10, 2022, 3:44pm 9

I really dislike the concept of addons in general although I do use them. I think it’s poor design to base your game around them and for better or worse addons are pretty much required for many aspects of the game. I do also understand that a lot of players enjoy the ability to customize their UI to their taste but it really should be possible to allow players some agency in that regard without external addons.

Unfortunately, that ship sailed many years ago. Addons are here to stay.

2 Likes

[Clark-1722524](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Clark-1722524) (Clark) February 10, 2022, 3:44pm 10

Hycendia:

> “Who is going to” – stop you right there bud — Blizzard, if they wish to continue relying their game on Addons so much to make it function in any sane form.
> 
>

Ok then accept paying $20 or$25 monthly subs then for their in house addon client

1 Like
[GhostCatX-1938579](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/GhostCatX-1938579) (GhostCatX) February 10, 2022, 3:46pm 11

Because it’s distasteful at most, and that’s the issue.

They aren’t even doing anything wrong, it’s just against what people want.

They own the repository, and for 3rd party apps like WoWUp to use it to hook into the back end and aggregate those addon in another client, Overwolf has to let them. The addons themselves are free. You can get them without using any client at all.

The Overwolf implementation of this is also free. The ads are another story but Curse did that before too. They only let you update one addon at a time unless you had premium. Almost the same deal here.

I personally hate this. I do think Blizzard needs to step back and take a 10,000 foot view of what is going on with addons and create a new policy.

1 Like
